correctness.rationale: For each primitive SRG, two positive nontrivial edge-vector projector norms generate exactly two new simple positive eigenvalues under every nonzero perturbation of a positive edge conductance. The explicit projectors give nonzero components at precisely the asserted vertices; a nonempty same-signature vertex set proves all inherited modes visible to every actuator. Thus Krylov dimension is 3 or 5 as claimed; exact combinatorial counting gives 2(k−λ). The proof covers all admissible graphs, edges, actuators and positive conductances. Reproduced 14846 rational checks corroborate 8 finite graph examples; they are not extrapolated to universality.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2017 edge perturbation work provides the spectral eigenvalue equation, but not the every-vertex single-actuator rank partition; the latter requires independent calculations of eigenvector visibility at all vertices and a nonvanishing argument for both inherited eigenspaces. The 2012 and 2015 control papers provide general PBH/walk-matrix methodology or uncontrollable baseline SRG statements, not the result. The new complete rank table and graph-parameter-only census are not immediate stated consequences of those sources, and the inspected primary literature and accessible published research abstracts revealed no matching theorem. Risk remains of an unpublished/implicit equivalent derivation in the 2017 paper or related sources.
residual_risks: The near-identical spectral setup of arxiv:1710.02181 could permit a more immediate implicit derivation than the differences in stated theorems suggest. The new every-vertex controllability conclusion remains the asserted contribution.
Unindexed or inaccessible specialist work on strongly regular walk matrices may contain equivalent vertex-rank formulas.

value.rationale: The exact single-actuator reachable dimension is a physically motivated network-design invariant. The theorem gives a complete, parameter-only classification of where and by how much a local edge-conductance defect improves control, with no hidden exceptional weights and identical counts for nonisomorphic SRGs with matching parameters. It distinguishes full control only for the five-cycle from intrinsic five-mode caps for all larger primitive SRGs.
